shouldFix.title: Finding-object identity is not type-total, so empty and null IDs pass the governing lineage checks
evidence: v19 makes the severity members type-total and validates finding severity, but neither extractor branch requires object.id to be present, a string, non-empty, trimmed, or compatible with the colon-delimited FromVN encoding. uniqueness only rejects two equal ids; it does not validate one id.
A combined-schema probe with findings=[{id:'',severity:'SHOULD-FIX'}], blockers=0, shouldFix=1, advisories=0 is recognized, passes the independent severity counts, and extracts ('',SHOULD-FIX).

The empty-id probe passes the full governing chain: a register row with id='', severity SHOULD-FIX, and disposition REPAIRED matches the extracted pair; a repair string ': addressed' has canonical prefix '' under fromVnIdExtractionRule and therefore satisfies FromVN equality.

The severity-array branch also accepts advisories=[{id:null,severity:'ADVISORY'}], derives (null,ADVISORY), and can match a null-id ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING register row without any FromVN entry. Thus the gap is not limited to the empty-string delimiter edge.

All 64 actual registered v8-v18 finding ids are globally unique, non-empty strings, colon-free, and match the uppercase/digit/hyphen convention. Every current lane and repair prefix reproduces, so the defect is confined to the standing mechanical rule and is SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: The mechanism can certify a frozen blocker or SHOULD-FIX with no addressable identity as repaired through an empty prefix, or preserve a null advisory id that downstream tools may treat as missing. This defeats deterministic finding lineage and reopens omission/aliasing behavior at the item boundary even though the container schemas are now fail-closed.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Require every extracted finding object and every register finding to contain an id that is a non-empty canonical string. At minimum reject absent, null, boolean, numeric, object, array, empty, whitespace-only, and colon-containing ids; preferably state the corpus grammar explicitly. Require each FromVN canonical prefix to satisfy the same rule before equality, so an empty or noncanonical prefix cannot represent a repaired finding.
